rule: Don't use Inter/Roboto/Arial/Open Sans as primary heading font. These are AI-generation defaults that signal generic output.
test_question: Is the heading font one of the 'AI default' set?
violation_example: h1 in Inter — looks like every ChatGPT-generated landing page
fix_example: Plus Jakarta Sans / Outfit / Manrope / DM Sans / Geist as primary

rule: No pure #000000 or #FFFFFF or #888888. Pure values look flat and synthetic. Use tinted neutrals.
test_question: Are any background/text colors pure black/white/grey?
violation_example: Background: #000000 with text: #FFFFFF — harsh and generic

rule: Avoid default #6366F1 indigo / #3B82F6 blue as primary accent. These are the most common AI-generated brand colors.
test_question: Is the primary accent a default Tailwind blue/indigo/violet?
violation_example: Primary button in #6366F1 — indistinguishable from every SaaS template
fix_example: Distinctive brand purple #461499 or custom-mixed accent

rule: No purple-to-blue or pink-to-purple background gradients. Max 1 decorative gradient per page.
test_question: Does the page use a generic gradient hero or multiple decorative gradients?
violation_example: Hero background: linear-gradient(135deg #667eea #764ba2) — the most overused AI gradient
fix_example: Solid dark bg with subtle texture or single-color gradient with brand tint

rule: Not everything needs a card wrapper. Use typography hierarchy and spacing to create structure. Cards should group genuinely related content.
test_question: Could I remove this card border/background and the content still makes sense via spacing alone?
violation_example: Every paragraph and icon wrapped in its own rounded-corner card — visual noise
fix_example: Use section padding + heading hierarchy. Reserve cards for genuinely grouped content

rule: Never nest a card inside a card. Flatten the visual hierarchy. If content needs sub-grouping use spacing or subtle dividers.
test_question: Is there a bordered/shadowed element inside another bordered/shadowed element?
violation_example: Feature card containing a nested stats card with its own border and shadow
fix_example: Flatten: remove inner card styling. Use background tint or divider line instead

rule: Don't use identical column grids for every section. Vary the rhythm: 2-col then 3-col then full-width then asymmetric.
test_question: Are 3+ consecutive sections using the same column layout?
violation_example: Six sections all using 3-column equal-width grids — monotonous scroll
fix_example: Alternate: 2-col split → 3-col cards → full-width quote → asymmetric bento

rule: Border-radius > 16px on non-pill elements looks toy-like. Buttons: 6-12px. Cards: 8-16px. Only pills/tags use full rounding.
test_question: Are cards or containers using border-radius > 16px?
violation_example: Content cards with border-radius: 24px — looks like a children's app
fix_example: Cards: rounded-xl (12px). Buttons: rounded-lg (8px). Only badges use rounded-full

rule: Every visual effect must answer: what does this help the user understand or do? No answer = delete the effect.
test_question: Can I explain what this gradient/glow/animation helps the user accomplish?
violation_example: Floating gradient orbs that don't relate to any content or guide attention
fix_example: Glow behind CTA to draw attention to the action (justified). Random particle animation (unjustified — delete)

rule: If the user can understand the purpose via layout/icon/position alone — the explanatory text is redundant. Delete it.
test_question: If I remove this text does the user lose any understanding?
violation_example: Label 'Click here to submit' on a clearly styled Submit button
fix_example: Remove redundant label. The button style + position + 'Submit' text is sufficient

rule: Never use emoji as functional UI icons. Emoji render differently across OS/browser and look unprofessional.
test_question: Are any interactive elements using emoji instead of SVG icons?
violation_example: 📧 as the contact link icon — renders differently on every platform
fix_example: Use Lucide/Heroicons/Phosphor SVG icon set for consistent rendering

rule: Shadows imply physical elevation. Only use shadow when an element genuinely floats above others (modals dropdowns cards).
test_question: Does this shadow represent real elevation or is it decorative?
violation_example: Box-shadow on every section container — nothing actually 'floats'
fix_example: Reserve shadow for cards that overlap content + modals + dropdowns. Flat sections get no shadow

rule: Decorative continuous animation with no user trigger is distraction. Animation should respond to user action or convey state change.
test_question: Does this animation fire without user interaction AND serve no informational purpose?
violation_example: Floating particles / pulsing circles running continuously in the background
fix_example: Remove or tie to scroll position / hover / load-once. Background texture (static) instead of animation

rule: Avoid the default AI hero: centered h1 + centered subtitle + single CTA + gradient background. Differentiate with asymmetry or content.
test_question: Does this hero look like it could be any product's landing page?
violation_example: Centered 'Welcome to Our Platform' + 'Get Started' button on gradient — could be anything
fix_example: Asymmetric hero with product visual + specific value prop + social proof element

rule: Empty space is a design feature not a bug. Don't fill every pixel. Generous padding signals premium quality.
test_question: Am I adding this element because it improves the page or because the space 'felt empty'?
violation_example: Cramming a testimonial carousel into the gap between pricing and footer because 'there was space'
fix_example: Let the spacing breathe. py-24 between sections. Whitespace = premium signal
